stories.title: Trump Awards Presidential Medal of Freedom to Rudy Giuliani
stories.summary: President Donald Trump has awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom to Rudy Giuliani, the former mayor of New York City, recognizing his leadership during the 9/11 attacks. Giuliani, who has been a close ally of Trump and served as his personal lawyer, has faced controversy for his role in efforts to overturn the 2020 presidential election results. The award ceremony took place in the Oval Office.

stories.title: Trump Pardons Turkeys Freedom and Feathers at White House Ceremony
stories.summary: President Trump held the annual Thanksgiving turkey pardon ceremony at the White House, granting pardons to two turkeys named Freedom and Feathers. This tradition allows the birds to skip Thanksgiving dinner and continue living. The turkeys were introduced prior to the ceremony, where they were housed at a hotel in Washington.

stories.title: Huawei Convicted of Trade Secrets Theft, Acquitted of Racketeering Charges
stories.summary: A federal jury in Brooklyn found Huawei guilty on 10 of 12 counts related to stealing trade secrets and deceiving banks about its business in Iran. However, the company was acquitted of the more serious charge of engaging in a criminal racketeering conspiracy. The verdict concludes a months-long trial.

stories.title: Senegal Restored as 2025 AFCON Champions Following CAS Ruling
stories.summary: The Court of Arbitration for Sport has reinstated Senegal as the winners of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations, overturning a previous decision that awarded the title to Morocco. The ruling confirmed Senegal's victory over Morocco in the final held in January, where Senegal won 1-0 after extra time. Morocco has expressed its intention to pursue further legal action in response to this decision.

stories.title: Huawei Found Guilty of Conspiracy to Steal Trade Secrets and Bank Fraud
stories.summary: A U.S. jury has convicted Huawei Technologies of conspiracy to steal trade secrets and bank fraud. The company was accused of stealing technology from U.S. firms, violating U.S. sanctions by doing business with countries like Iran and North Korea, and making false statements to government officials and banks. This conviction represents a significant legal challenge for the Chinese tech giant.

stories.title: Hostage Situation in Cartagena, Colombia Following Failed Robbery
stories.summary: Armed men have taken at least 25 hostages in a supermarket in Cartagena, Colombia, after a failed attempt to rob an armored truck. Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella described the assailants as 'common criminals' and confirmed that police and military forces have been deployed to manage the situation as it unfolds.

stories.title: Nicolas Sarkozy and Carla Bruni to Stand Trial for Witness Tampering
stories.summary: Former French President Nicolas Sarkozy and his wife, Carla Bruni, are scheduled to face trial in 2027. They are facing allegations of criminal conspiracy and witness tampering related to illegal campaign funding from Libya during Sarkozy's 2007 election campaign. This follows Sarkozy's imprisonment last year for separate charges.

stories.summary: Representative Jimmy Gomez, a Democrat from California, announced his resignation effective December 1 after a House Ethics panel found evidence of sexual misconduct. This resignation follows Gomez's loss in the recent reelection bid and marks him as the second California Democrat to resign this year over similar allegations.

stories.title: Saurav Das Barred from UK Flight, Criticizes Indian Government
stories.summary: Saurav Das, a leader of the Citizens for Justice and Peace (CJP), was prevented from boarding a flight to the UK due to his passport being flagged by immigration authorities at Delhi airport. He received a notice from the Chennai Regional Passport Office shortly before his scheduled departure, but the government has not provided any explanation for the action taken against him.
